**Ferdinand I** ([Italian](/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language"): *Ferdinando I*; 12 January 1751 – 4 January 1825) was [King of the Two Sicilies](/wiki/Kingdom_of_the_Two_Sicilies "Kingdom of the Two Sicilies") from 1816 until his death. Before that he had been, since 1759, [King of Naples](/wiki/King_of_Naples "King of Naples") as **Ferdinand IV** and [King of Sicily](/wiki/King_of_Sicily "King of Sicily") as **Ferdinand III**. He was deposed twice from the throne of Naples: once by the revolutionary [Parthenopean Republic](/wiki/Parthenopean_Republic "Parthenopean Republic") for six months in 1799, and again by a [French invasion](/wiki/Invasion_of_Naples_(1806) "Invasion of Naples (1806)") in 1806, before being restored in 1815 at the end of the [Napoleonic Wars](/wiki/Napoleonic_Wars "Napoleonic Wars").

Ferdinand was born in Naples as the third son of [King Charles VII](/wiki/Charles_III_of_Spain "Charles III of Spain") and [Queen Maria Amalia](/wiki/Maria_Amalia_of_Saxony "Maria Amalia of Saxony"). In August 1759, Charles succeeded his half-brother [Ferdinand VI of Spain](/wiki/Ferdinand_VI_of_Spain "Ferdinand VI of Spain") as King Charles III, but treaty provisions made him ineligible to hold all three crowns. On 6 October, he abdicated his Neapolitan and Sicilian titles in favour of his third son, Ferdinand, because his eldest son [Philip](/wiki/Infante_Philip,_Duke_of_Calabria "Infante Philip, Duke of Calabria") had been excluded from succession due to intellectual disability and his second son [Charles](/wiki/Charles_IV_of_Spain "Charles IV of Spain") was heir-apparent to the Spanish throne. Ferdinand was the founder of the cadet [House of Bourbon-Two Sicilies](/wiki/House_of_Bourbon-Two_Sicilies "House of Bourbon-Two Sicilies").

After staying at number one for fourteen nonconsecutive weeks, it joined four other songs in a tie as the [second longest running number-one song in US chart history](/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones"), behind Carey's own 1995 collaboration with [Boyz II Men](/wiki/Boyz_II_Men "Boyz II Men") titled "[One Sweet Day](/wiki/One_Sweet_Day "One Sweet Day")". *Billboard* listed it as the "song of the decade" and the fifteenth most popular song of all time. Additionally, it broke several airplay records, gathering both the largest one-day and one-week audiences in history. "We Belong Together" also topped the charts in Australia; and reached the top five in more than ten countries, including Ireland, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Spain and the United Kingdom.

The song's music video was filmed as a two-part story with "[It's Like That](/wiki/It%27s_Like_That_(Mariah_Carey_song) "It's Like That (Mariah Carey song)")", which featured Carey at her bachelorette party. The video for "We Belong Together" is a continuation, focusing on Carey's wedding to a powerful older man and ending with the singer eloping with her younger ex-lover (played by actor [Wentworth Miller](/wiki/Wentworth_Miller "Wentworth Miller") of the TV show *[Prison Break](/wiki/Prison_Break "Prison Break")*). Rumors arose of the video's connection to her 1993 marriage to then-[Sony Music](/wiki/Sony_Music "Sony Music") CEO [Tommy Mottola](/wiki/Tommy_Mottola "Tommy Mottola"), as they did for Carey’s 1997 video for the song “Honey”. Carey performed the song on several award shows and television appearances around the world, namely [MTV Movie Awards]
